faqs.question: Is it too late to send a Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card?
faqs.answer: For a posted card, yes, if you are outside the recipient's city. India Post's own norm is 4–5 days to the rest of the country, so a card for Monday 14 September 2026 needed posting by about 7 September. A link or an image still arrives in seconds.

faqs.question: What is the last date to post a Ganesh Chaturthi card in India?
faqs.answer: Counting back from 14 September 2026 using India Post's Speed Post norms, roughly 7 September for a cross-country card, 9 September metro to metro, and 12 September inside the same city. Sundays and gazetted holidays do not count, and Branch Office bookings add a day.

faqs.question: How much does a Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card cost delivered?
faqs.answer: About ₹146 to ₹546 if you post it — ₹99 to ₹499 for the card plus ₹47 Speed Post anywhere in India, or ₹19 local, with GST extra on the postage. An image or a page link costs nothing to send.

faqs.question: What should I write in a Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card?
faqs.answer: Name the person, then the wish. "Ganpati Bappa Morya" and "Ganesh Chaturthi ki hardik shubhkamnaye" are the two lines almost everyone recognises, and one specific sentence about the person is worth more than three borrowed ones.

faqs.question: Can I put someone's name on a Ganesh Chaturthi card online?
faqs.answer: Yes, either burned into a JPEG by an online photo editor or held as live text on a page. The difference matters: a name in a JPEG cannot be corrected after you send it, while a name on a page can.

faqs.question: Is a digital Ganesh Chaturthi greeting as good as a printed card?
faqs.answer: For reaching someone today, it is better, and it is the only option once the posting window has shut. For being kept, the printed card wins — it is an object on a shelf for the ten days to Anant Chaturdashi, and a link is not.

faqs.question: Does a forwarded Ganesh Chaturthi image count as a greeting card?
faqs.answer: Recipients treat it as traffic rather than as a gift, because a forward makes no choice about who receives it. Hill and Dunbar's card study is the reason why: writing a card is a decision about who is inside your circle of roughly 150 people.

faqs.question: What size is a Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card for posting?
faqs.answer: India Post caps a Speed Post document at 420 × 297 × 24 mm and 500 g, which comfortably covers an A4 folded card. Anything thicker or heavier moves to a parcel rate and a slower delivery norm.

faqs.question: Which is faster, Speed Post or ordinary post, for a festival card?
faqs.answer: Speed Post, by two to three days on longer routes. The Citizens' Charter gives Speed Post 4–5 days to the rest of the country against 5–6 days for First Class Mail, and 1–2 days local against 2 days.

faqs.question: When is Ganesh Chaturthi in 2026 and when does it end?
faqs.answer: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 falls on Monday 14 September, and the festival runs to Anant Chaturdashi visarjan on Friday 25 September. That ten-day span is why a physical card still has a job after the first day.

faqs.question: Do most people really leave festival greetings to the last day?
faqs.answer: In the one festival we have measured, yes. Of 89 rakhi pages built for Raksha Bandhan 2026, 49.4% were built on the day itself and the median lead time was 0 days — but that is a different, one-day festival, and 89 is a small sample.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi Greeting Card: What Still Arrives In Time

A Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card comes in four forms — a printed card you post, one you make by hand, a name-style image from an online photo editor, or a link to a page — and only the printed one has a deadline you can miss. Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 falls on Monday 14 September. India Post's own service standard for Speed Post is 4–5 days to the rest of the country, so a posted card had to be in the box by about 7 September; the other three arrive in seconds.

That gap matters, because the one festival we have actually measured says senders do not plan: of 89 rakhi pages built for Raksha Bandhan 2026, 49.4% were built on the festival day itself, and the median lead time was 0 days. Meanwhile 49.6% of our 46,005 recorded page views come from a phone. Below are the real posting dates, the delivered cost of each format, and where a printed card still beats a link.

## What a Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card is: four formats, one deadline

A Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card is any object or file carrying a Ganesh Chaturthi wish addressed to a named person — usually "Ganpati Bappa Morya" or "Ganesh Chaturthi ki hardik shubhkamnaye", with the sender's and recipient's names on it. The formats differ on exactly one thing: whether the greeting has to travel physically.

A printed card travels, so it inherits constraints: India Post caps a Speed Post document at 420 × 297 × 24 mm and 500 g, charges for it, and delivers it on a published schedule. An image file and a page link inherit none of that, and that single difference decides what you can still do four days out.

## The posting deadline for 14 September 2026 was 7 September cross-country

India Post publishes its delivery norms in the [Citizens' Charter of the Department of Posts](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/documents/CitizenCharter2021.pdf): Speed Post is 1–2 days local, 1–3 days metro to metro, 1–4 days between state capitals or within a state, and 4–5 days to the rest of the country. Sundays and gazetted holidays are excluded, and anything booked or delivered at a Branch Office takes one extra day.

Counted back from Monday 14 September 2026, the last safe posting day was about Monday 7 September for a cross-country card, Wednesday 9 September metro to metro, and Friday 12 September inside the same city. Ordinary post is slower again: the same charter allows First Class Mail — letters, postcards and inland letter cards — 5–6 days to the rest of the country.

After 9 September the cross-country window is shut. That is not a reason to send nothing; it is a reason to stop shopping for a card.

## Four ways to send a Ganesh Chaturthi greeting card, priced

### 1. A printed card bought off a shelf

Folded religious-festival cards were listed on Indian retail shelves at roughly ₹99–₹499 when we checked the shopping results for this query on 9 September 2026, with wooden and laser-cut cards above that. Nothing is editable once it is posted, and you learn whether it arrived only from the tracking number.

### 2. A card made by hand

Free if you already own card stock and sketch pens, and it carries more weight per rupee than anything else here. It costs the one thing a late sender has run out of — an evening — and it still has to be delivered.

### 3. A name-style image from an online photo editor

A Ganesh image with the recipient's name burned into the JPEG, built in a browser in a couple of minutes and sent on WhatsApp for nothing. It lands instantly and it is final: once the file is delivered, a misspelt name stays misspelt in their gallery.

### 4. A shareable page with a link

A page the recipient opens on their phone, with the names and photo held as live text instead of baked into pixels. It costs nothing, arrives in seconds, and stays editable after the link has gone out.

## Card against page: ₹146 and five working days versus ₹0 and seconds

Delivered cost and delivered time for the same wish, with our own measurement in the last column.

| Format | Cost delivered | Reaches them in | What we measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Printed card, Speed Post to the rest of the country | ₹146–₹546 (₹99–₹499 card + ₹47 postage, GST extra) | 4–5 working days | No first-party data; the 7 September cut-off has passed |
| Printed card, Speed Post inside the same city | ₹118–₹518 (₹99–₹499 card + ₹19 postage, GST extra) | 1–2 working days | No first-party data; same-city cut-off is 12 September |
| Name-style image sent on WhatsApp | ₹0 | Seconds | 49.6% of our 46,005 page views come from a phone |
| Shareable page with a link | ₹0 | Seconds | Median 5.4 hours from a festival page's first save to its last edit (n=89) |

Speed Post rates come from India Post's own [domestic Speed Post tariff](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/mailproducts/premiumservices) — ₹47 countrywide, ₹19 local, up to 50 g, GST extra. The table is why the "which is nicer" argument is academic: past 9 September, two of the four rows are gone.

## What the printed card does that no page can: 2,984 cards across 43 households

R. A. Hill and R. I. M. Dunbar had people fill in a questionnaire while they were actually addressing their Christmas cards, and collected [43 completed returns covering 2,984 cards](https://rahill.webspace.durham.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/sites/207/2021/04/Hill-and-Dunbar-2003.pdf) for *Human Nature* in 2003. The mean household sent 68.19 cards, range 11–149. Those lists mapped a social network averaging 153.5 people, of whom roughly 21% were relatives.

That is the printed card's real function, and it is not aesthetic. Writing a card is a decision about who is inside your circle of about 150, made one envelope at a time, and the recipient can feel it. A greeting forwarded into a group of 200 makes no such decision, which is why it reads as traffic rather than as a gift.

The card is also an object.

The scholarship on greeting cards treats them as socio-cultural and historical heritage rather than as a means of transmitting information — a 2022 [open-access review of greeting-card research](https://doi.org/10.18372/2415-8151.25.16797) makes exactly that point about the postal card of the late nineteenth century. A card props up on a shelf for the ten days to Anant Chaturdashi on 25 September. A link does not.

Be careful with the Hill and Dunbar numbers, though: 43 British households at Christmas is not 89 Indian senders at a Hindu festival, and neither sample is large.

## Why 67% pick the easier channel, and what our 89 rakhi pages say

Asked to reconnect with someone from their past, [67% of 200 participants said they would rather do it by email than by phone](https://www.kumar-amit.com/s/Kumar-Epley-in-press-Its-surprisingly-nice-to-hear-you-JEPG.pdf) — while simultaneously predicting they would form a stronger bond by phone. When the researchers ran it, voice produced stronger bonds and no more awkwardness than text (Amit Kumar and Nicholas Epley, *Journal of Experimental Psychology: General*, 2020). People reliably pick the lower-effort channel and misprice the richer one.

Our own numbers point the same way on timing rather than on medium.

Across both rakhi collections, n = 89 pages: 6.7% were built four or more days ahead, 5.6% two to three days ahead, 27.0% the day before, 49.4% on the day itself, and 11.2% after the festival had passed. Not one was built more than seven days ahead. Of the 79 that landed in time, 86.1% were finished within 24 hours of the festival.

Two things have to be said about that measurement. **It is Raksha Bandhan 2026, not Ganesh Chaturthi** — a different festival, and a one-day one, where Ganesh Chaturthi runs ten days to Anant Chaturdashi. The shape is suggestive for this festival, not measured for it.

**And n = 89 is small.** Do not read a per-template or per-region rate off it, and do not project a count of Ganesh pages from it: occasion-dated pages are 144 of our 3,894 pages, 3.7%, and we have no Ganesh page-creation data at all.

## When a link is the wrong answer, and where our own page falls short

A link fails outright when the recipient cannot open one. 49.6% of our views arrive on a phone, but a household on a landline is 0% of that, and a printed card is the only format that works there. A mandap noticeboard, a society gate and a hand-delivered card to a neighbour all want paper too — and if the recipient is in the same room, a link is a strange thing to hand them.

The honest limit on our side is bigger than that. Our Ganesh Chaturthi page is built but not yet published on the site, so nothing in this post links to it and nothing here depends on you opening it. If you want a SubhSandesh page today, [browse the live templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates); the closest in shape to a festival greeting card are the [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) and the [animated shaadi card](https://subhsandesh.in/shaadi-card), both of which put names, a photo and a message behind one link.

And a page is worse than a card at one thing a card is unbeatable at: being kept. Nobody puts a URL in a drawer for twenty years.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

## Sources

- India Post, [Citizens' Charter of the Department of Posts](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/documents/CitizenCharter2021.pdf), 2021 — Speed Post 1–2 days local to 4–5 days countrywide; First Class Mail 5–6 days.
- India Post, [Domestic Speed Post Document](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/mailproducts/premiumservices) — ₹47 nationwide, ₹19 local, up to 50 g, GST extra.
- Hill and Dunbar, [Social Network Size in Humans](https://rahill.webspace.durham.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/sites/207/2021/04/Hill-and-Dunbar-2003.pdf), *Human Nature* 14(1), 2003 — 2,984 Christmas cards, 43 households.
- Kumar and Epley, [It's Surprisingly Nice to Hear You](https://www.kumar-amit.com/s/Kumar-Epley-in-press-Its-surprisingly-nice-to-hear-you-JEPG.pdf), *J. Exp. Psychol. General*, 2020 — 67% of 200 chose email.
- Davydova, [Thematic analysis of greeting-card scholarship](https://doi.org/10.18372/2415-8151.25.16797), *Theory and Practice of Design* 1(25), 2022 — open access.

Two do not: India Post's Citizens' Charter delivery norms and Kumar and Epley on channel choice could both sit unchanged in the sibling `ganesh-chaturthi-invitation-maker` post, which faces the same printed-versus-digital deadline question. auditReport.honestAssessment: The one thing here no competitor publishes is the deadline. Every page ranking for `ganesh chaturthi greeting card` — Canva, Adobe Express, PosterMyWall, 123Greetings, the egreetings.gov.in portal, Amazon and woodgeekstore, the Times of India listicle — assumes the reader has time, and not one states a posting cut-off, a delivered cost or what to do once the window has shut. This post gives 7 September for a cross-country card against a 14 September festival, ₹146–₹546 delivered against ₹0, and pairs that with a first-party measurement nobody else can print: 49.4% of 89 measured festival senders acted on the day itself, median lead time 0 days. The format risk is real and should not be hidden. The Q1 SERP is not an informational SERP — DuckDuckGo's top 10 has zero informational results and Google's top 13 has exactly one, with no AI Overview on either query — so a 1,770-word article is competing against design tools for a query whose dominant intent is 'give me the card now'. It should not be expected to displace Canva's gallery, and the honest ceiling is the last-minute-sender sliver plus answer-engine citation for the deadline and cost questions, where the post is the only page with numbers. Two further constraints: SubhSandesh's Ganesh Chaturthi template is built but not published, so this post has no on-topic template to convert to and links `/templates`, the Raksha Bandhan brother page and the shaadi card instead; and the live `ganesh-chaturthi-wishes-with-name` post declares this keyword and both of its folded secondaries in its own brief and `article.keywords`, which needs resolving at consolidation (see the research brief). Domain authority against Canva and Adobe is not something this post can close, and ranking takes months — no outcome is predicted here.
